GALLERY 01 · OUR FIRST DATE

Worth the Detour

Our first date started with a reservation I hadn’t actually made. I’d only joined the waitlist at National Kitchen by Violet Oon, so we had to find another plan.

We wandered through galleries, explored the foyer, and walked around the building looking for a restaurant that turned out to be inside it, just on another floor.

Eventually, there was Korean BBQ, two pork dishes, and us serving each other food. Then KOI, and an indoor booth where we sat side by side.

These are the five moments I keep coming back to.
GALLERY 02 · OUR SECOND DATE

The Next One

We planned to meet at Gardens by the Bay station. I was early and a little nervous, so I bought myself a coffee to calm down and a bottled tea for you. While I was buying it, you walked right past me. You waited for me at the bottom of the escalator.

We walked around Gardens by the Bay at sunset, and I complained far too much about the heat and the haze. We went up among the Supertrees like tourists, and it felt like we had forever to talk and look at the view. Up there, I finally found the courage to ask for our first photo together.

At dinner, the conversation flowed so easily. We shared our dishes, and you made the perfect bite for me. Afterwards, with no plan, we walked all the way to the food court at MBS, where you watched me eat an entire dessert by myself and we lost track of time talking about the most random things.

When it was time for you to go home, I rode the MRT with you, past my own station, because I didn’t want to leave. You gently rested your head on my shoulder, and that felt wonderful. At your station, when I said goodbye, you said we’d wait for the next one. So we did.

These are the five moments I keep coming back to.
GALLERY 03 · OUR THIRD DATE

Never Enough Time

We met on a Sunday afternoon. We’d planned it on short notice, because every time a date ended, there never seemed to be enough time. I got there first, took one look at the Molly Tea queue, and waited for you outside a shoe shop nearby.

You arrived with Molly Tea in its cute pink bag. I awkwardly admitted I was a bit hungry, and even though you weren’t, you came for malatang with me. We shared one big bowl, dry with no soup and full of lotus root, which we both liked, picking from it into our own small bowls. You watched me gobble mine down while you ate slowly and politely, and since they only took scan-to-pay, you covered dinner.

With no plan, we wandered into H&M Home and the clothes next door. I showed you a couple of outfits I liked, and you made fun of me. We stood there not knowing where to go, until I suggested the Singapore Art Museum. I didn’t understand most of the exhibits, but you were the most captivating thing there.

Then I insisted on taking public transport. The bus that came was a strange private one that only took cash, so I called a Grab back to my accommodation instead, slightly embarrassed. We kept chatting and decided we wanted matching Beyond the Vines bags, so we went and got the dumpling bags, along with an interesting tofu ice cream.

We ended with supper at Haidilao. You said you like seeing my excited face when I eat good hotpot. After the meal I moved to sit next to you, and we kept talking for what felt like hours.

These are the five moments I keep coming back to.
GALLERY 04 · OUR LAST DAY

Every Last Minute

On my last day, you came super early because you wanted to make the most of every last minute we had together. We went straight to the breakfast buffet. Once again you ate so little, and you made fun of me and my love of sambal, peanuts and anchovies.

Then work started bothering me. You stayed right beside me so patiently while I worked on my laptop. I felt bad that it wasn’t quality time, but you just sat there with me, so sweetly.

Afterwards I called a Grab, and it was one of the saddest car rides. I kept thinking about leaving you, and about the life we could have together. You handed me a booklet that said so much, and told me not to read it until later.

At the airport, you saw me off. We hugged one last time before I went through the gates, and it felt like a hug that would always be too short.

On the plane, I slowly read everything you wanted to tell me. It was the first time I’ve ever cried on a plane. I couldn’t stop thinking about you.

These are the five moments I keep coming back to.
